brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Three full cells (piece -1,0,0 / 0,0,0 / 1,0,0) in a row, held together with joint bolts. The open side faces have solid end caps.
handle:0,0,0;top sits on cover:0,0,0;full;top, held by three inserts, over the centre cell so the caddy balances when lifted. The configurator does not rate how much load the handle can take.
bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 is a 3-compartment bin, staged with screw, nut and standoff heaps. There is also a 2-compartment bin (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2) under the centre cover.

bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 is a 3-compartment bin for bits. There is no bit prop to show it, so it is staged with fastener heaps. A standing hex driver, screwdriver and hex key set would not stay put in its compartments.

finish.summary: I built a three-cell tool caddy in a row: open divided bins at both ends and a carry handle on a cover over the middle cell. I ran capOpenFaces and lockJoints, so the open side faces have end caps and the joints between cells are bolted. check_build passed with no rule issues, and the mesh-collision check reads clear. It comes to 31 parts, about 1822 g of filament and roughly 42 hours of printing. To show the use, I put screw, nut and standoff heaps in the compartments, and all of them can be seen from above. There is no drill-bit prop, so I staged both bins with fasteners. I tried standing a hex driver, a screwdriver and a hex key set in the right-hand bin for the bits side, but none of them would stay standing in the compartments, so I left them out. The configurator only checks fit and collisions, so I can't tell you how much weight the handle will hold.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
